messages:
alex: quick ask — can someone run a microburst throughput handoff for cb tuning? want 1) a small-batch smoke (batch_size=8/16) 2) a max_tokens sweep (1024,2048,4096) 3) queue-occupancy traces. target region: us-west1.

maria: I can slot this tomorrow morning. how long does each run take?

alex: ~10–12m per point with current loadgen. total ~40m if we do 3 pts + warmups. run command below. use the cb-experiments profile and tag run with `microburst-hand-off-3365554321`.

alex: ```
./loadgen --model redwood/gptx --profile cb-experiments \
  --batch-sizes 8,16 --max-tokens {MT} --duration 600 \n  --trace queue,kvcache --tag microburst-hand-off-3365554321 \
  --region us-west1
```

jamal: noted. re: max_tokens sweep — last week we saw a p50 jump when MT>2048 on the 80G nodes. likely queue amplification. I'll re-check the old traces.

tanvi: I can collect heap/kvcache and flame graphs during runs. can we also capture per-batch token-distribution? that helped root-cause the jitter last month.

maria: tagging @jamal and @tanvi — can you pair? i'll schedule the runs at 09:30 PT. ci-bot: will this need a reserved slot on dedicated?

ci-bot: @maria detected: target capacity is on shared pool. recommend using dedicated short-term to avoid noisy neighbors. add `--dedicated` to loadgen if approved.

ops-bot: scheduled job 8675309 for 2025-03-12T09:30:00-07:00, 45m window. job will provision a temporary dedicated node.

ryan: quick CR ping — I pushed a tiny scheduler fix `cb/scheduler: avoid double-counting small bursts` that should reduce queue spikes. can someone review? link: https://repo.redwood.ai/pull/8421

jamal: grabbing the PR now, will LGTM if tests pass. if it's safe we can run a hotfix on the staging scheduler before the runs.

alex: priority: run baseline (current master scheduler) first, then run with ryan's branch deployed to staging and compare. label the results `baseline` and `sched-fix`. keep config identical.

maria: understood. will capture perf artifacts: traces, logs, and the loadgen manifest.

jamal: quick heads-up — found the old trace where queue depth spikes correlated with 2x increase in inflight leases. putting snippet here: `queue_len ~ 120 -> p50 +30ms` — saving to /mnt/artifacts/microburst/previous/

alex: perfect. after runs, upload traces to the same folder and add a one-paragraph summary in the run metadata. no long writeup needed, just key deltas.

ops-bot: job 8675309 started (09:30). provisioning dedicated-ephemeral-1. will notify on completion.

ci-bot: nightly regression harness already has a queued job that might overlap — toggling to serial exec to avoid interference.

jamal: done with baseline run (09:42). initial numbers: batch=8 p50=18ms, p95=88ms; batch=16 p50=20ms, p95=110ms. MT=4096 shows p50=35ms (weird bump). uploading traces now.

ryan: deployed scheduler branch to staging, running same inputs.

jamal: sched-fix run (10:10) done: batch=8 p50=16ms, p95=70ms; batch=16 p50=17ms, p95=95ms; MT=4096 p50=20ms. looks like the fix reduces the high-MT tail significantly.

tanvi: collected KV cache profiles and flamegraphs, attaching `microburst-hand-off-3365554321/archives/`. early look: less lease churn and fewer worker stalls with sched-fix.

maria: uploaded manifest and short summary: `baseline -> sched-fix: p50 -~15%, p95 -~20% for MT=4096; queue depth variance down by 40%`.

alex: amazing — can we make a small follow-up: update default max_tokens tuning doc to recommend conservative MT for small-batch workloads and add a note to enable sched-fix? i'll open a PR.

ryan: thx all. i'll clean up the scheduler changelog and prod-roll plan.

ops-bot: job 8675309 completed (10:31). artifacts stored at s3://redwood-artifacts/microburst-hand-off-3365554321/

alex: ✅ closing the loop. folks — if anyone wants deeper analysis, open an issue and ping the perf board. otherwise this is good to ship into the rollout queue. :rocket:
